title: Pit Lane: Racing Sound Effects
shortText: 110 racing sound effects: five engines with seamless rev ladders, measured pass bys, a skid grid and a pit stop.
html:
Five race engines, every rev, every pass by

110 racing sound effects: five cars, each with its own engine, plus tyres, crashes, boost, the race and the pit stop.

Licence, up front

Royalty free. Commercial use. No attribution required. No revenue limit, no unit cap, no second licence to buy later if your game does well. Use it in as many projects as you like, on any platform. The one thing you may not do is resell the sounds themselves as a sound library. The plain language terms ship as LICENSE.txt, with a copy paste credit line if you want one.

Everything is synthesised from code. No recordings, no sample libraries, no third party clips, so there is no upstream licence behind this one and nobody can content ID claim these sounds against your project.

Hear it first

There is a free demo on this page: the whole muscle V8 (all five rev rungs, start, stop, limiter, both gear changes and all four pass bys), two skid surfaces at both slips, the race cues and the grandstand bed. Wire the V8's rungs to a rev counter before you pay.

An engine that answers the rev counter

One engine loop pitch shifted at runtime cannot follow a rev counter, because a real engine at high revs is not just faster, it is brighter. So every car ships a rev ladder: five seamless loops from idle to redline, each rendered from that car's own engine, so crossfading two neighbouring rungs never jumps timbre. Measured brightness, idle to redline:

  • Two stroke kart, one cylinder, thin and buzzing, screaming at the top: 684, 1129, 1926, 2820, 4915 Hz
  • Hot hatch four, a tuned inline four, even and eager, bright through the intake: 649, 1053, 1810, 3197, 4398 Hz
  • Muscle V8, cross plane, the uneven firing is the burble, loping at idle: 536, 921, 1510, 2492, 4270 Hz
  • Turbo rally four, a turbo four, the whistle climbing with the revs: 681, 1094, 1829, 3135, 4478 Hz
  • Electric racer, an inverter whine with a straight cut gear singing above it: 706, 1218, 1975, 3193, 4849 Hz

Each car also ships its start, stop and rev limiter (a seamless loop, with the crackle of unburnt fuel), and the combustion cars a gear up and gear down; the electric racer ships a launch and a regen instead. Every step of every ladder in the pack rises by at least 8 percent in brightness, measured off the files.

Pass bys whose pitch drop is physics, and measured

Twenty pass bys: every car at 79, 137, 209, 288 km/h. Each one is rendered by moving the car's own engine past a listener and computing, sample by sample, when the sound left the car, so the drop in pitch is the travel time of the sound itself, and the level and air absorption follow the same distance. The drop was then measured off the shipped files: every one sits within 0.9 percent of what the speed predicts, from about two semitones at the slowest to between 8.0 and 8.2 at the fastest. The same engines rendered standing still read no shift at all, so the drop comes from the motion and not from the measurement. 20 of 20 pass by claims hold, and the figures ship as passby_proof.json.

Tyres as a grid

Ten seamless skid loops: five surfaces (asphalt, gravel, dirt, wet tarmac, ice) by two kinds of slip (sliding while still rolling, and locked wheels). Pick the row from the surface under the wheel and the column from how hard the player is braking. Every cell is measurably its own loop on both axes.

The rest of the race

  • Collisions by force: a tap, a hit, a crash and a wreck into a barrier, each longer than the last, plus bodywork scraping along it.
  • Boost: turbo spool, blow off valve, anti lag pops, a nitrous burst.
  • The race: countdown and go, a start light, lap and best lap, checkpoint, a wrong way warning loop, the finish line. Short UI tones, not music.
  • Pit stop: the wheel gun on five nuts, the air jack up and down, a refuelling loop.
  • Ambience: grandstand, pit garage, rain on the circuit, a night street circuit, a rally stage in a forest.

Measured apart from Haulage

If you also own our vehicle and machine pack Haulage, you do not get the same engine twice. Every Pit Lane rev rung was compared with every Haulage engine and machine rung, 1050 pairs, by the shape of the spectrum with pitch shifts allowed, so a transposed copy cannot hide. All 1050 clear the line a transposed copy measures under. Honestly, the closest pair (two engines idling) clears it by 7 percent.

Fit

  • WAV and OGG for every file, 16 bit, 44.1 kHz, mono.
  • 47 seamless loops with sample accurate loop points in both formats; a file ends in _loop if and only if it loops.
  • One loudness band: the inner 80 percent of the pack sits inside 0.28 dB.
  • Import notes for Unity, Godot, GameMaker, Unreal and the web, including how to crossfade a rev ladder.
  • pack_proof.json ships with the pack: 1048 checks, 0 failed.

Honest limits

These are synthesised engines, not recordings of real cars, and no car here is a licensed model. The measurements above are signal measurements, not a claim that it sounds good. That is what the free demo is for.

AI disclosure, stated truthfully: the code that generates these sounds was written with AI assistance. The sounds themselves are self contained procedural synthesis, resonant bodies and filters evaluated in code, with no generative audio model at any point. The cover and store images are drawn by code written with AI assistance.

More from the same studio

  • Haulage: Vehicle and Machine SFX, trucks, vans, a motorbike, a tractor and twelve machines under load, each with its own load ladder.
  • The full CSAF catalogue, sound packs, tilesets, sprites, music and tools.
